_about: How to verify and fix each preflight check, like the SE demo kit's preflight help. Keyed by check ID; an ID ending in -* matches a prefix (zia-read-* covers every ZIA area). Shown under each check as 'How to verify'. A key starting with * matches the end of an ID (*-present). 'action' adds a button that does the fix in the console.

keychain.what: The kit writes, reads and deletes a test value in this computer's keychain.
keychain.why: API client secrets, the provisioning key and test users' passwords live only in the keychain, never in files.
verify: Mac: Keychain Access opens and the login keychain is unlocked.
Windows: Credential Manager opens.
fix: Mac: unlock the login keychain (Keychain Access > File > Unlock).
Linux: install and start a keyring service (gnome-keyring or KWallet).

connect.what: The POV's API client signs in to the tenant.
connect.why: Nothing else can be checked or built without it.
verify: Administration > API > OneAPI > API Clients lists the client, and its client ID matches the one in Connect.
fix: Check the vanity domain, client ID and secret in Connect.
A lost secret: create a new one on the client and enter it in Connect.

zia-read-*.what: The kit lists one ZIA area (rules, categories, groups...) with the API client.
zia-read-*.why: The kit reads each area before planning, to find the customer's own objects and keep clear of them.
verify: Open the POV's API client: Internet Access (ZIA) is listed with at least view access.
fix: Give the client view access to this ZIA area (the role spec lists them all).

zia-activation.what: The kit reads ZIA's activation status.
zia-activation.why: ZIA changes take effect only when activated, and activation applies everyone's pending changes. The kit never activates someone else's work.
verify: The console's Activation menu shows no pending changes.
fix: Ask the admin to activate or discard their pending changes.

zia-names.what: The kit looks for objects in the tenant with the names the POV would use, that aren't this POV's.
zia-names.why: The kit never takes over or overwrites an object it didn't make.
verify: The detail lists each taken name and whether another POV on this laptop owns it.
fix: Give this POV its own prefix (Use prefix ZPOV2 on the Apply step, or `pov-kit set prefix ZPOV2`), then approve the new change list.
Or remove the other POV first (Handover).

zia-pilot.what: The kit looks for the pilot group the POV's rules will apply to.
zia-pilot.why: Every POV rule applies to the pilot group only, so nobody else in the company is affected.
verify: Pilot users shows the group, or the POV makes its own.
fix: Choose who tests in the Pilot users step.

zid-read.what: The kit lists ZIdentity users and groups.
zid-read.why: The POV can make its own pilot group and test users in ZIdentity, and checks pilot users' entitlements there.
verify: The POV's API client lists ZIdentity with view access (and user management, if the POV makes its group).
fix: Give the client ZIdentity access from the role spec, or name an existing pilot group instead (Pilot users step).

id-entitlements.what: For each pilot user, the kit reads ZIdentity's service entitlements.
id-entitlements.why: Unentitled users aren't sent to ZIA, so the POV's rules never see their traffic.
verify: The entitlements page (search: Entitlement) lists the pilot group under Internet & SaaS.
fix: Entitle the pilot group to Internet & SaaS (a step for the customer's admin).

id-read.what: The kit reads who the pilot users are, across products.
id-read.why: It needs them to scope every rule and check the users exist.
verify: The detail says what couldn't be read.
fix: Give the API client view access to ZIdentity and ZIA users (role spec).

id-zia-group.what: The kit checks each named pilot user is a member of the pilot group.
id-zia-group.why: The POV's rules apply only to members, so a user outside the group isn't part of the POV.
verify: The customer's directory lists each pilot user in the group.
fix: Add them to the group in the customer's directory (it syncs to Zscaler).
id-zia-group.retest: Run checks again (after the directory syncs).

zpa-customer-id.what: The kit looks for the ZPA customer ID saved in Connect.
zpa-customer-id.why: ZPA's API needs it, even through OneAPI.
verify: Administration > API > Legacy API > Private Access API > Copy ID shows it.
fix: Paste it into Connect > ZPA customer ID.

zpa-read.what: The kit reads ZPA with the customer ID.
zpa-read.why: Planning ZPA needs the tenant's segments, groups and certificates.
verify: The customer ID in Connect matches Copy ID digit for digit, and the client has view access to ZPA.
fix: Copy the customer ID again (a 404 means it's wrong or cut short).
Add ZPA access to the API client.

zpa-cert.what: The kit looks for ZPA's connector enrollment certificate.
zpa-cert.why: The POV's provisioning key needs it to enroll App Connectors.
verify: Every ZPA tenant has one named Connector (search: Enrollment Certificates).
fix: Check the API client's view access to ZPA certificates.

zpa-overlap.what: The kit checks the POV app's domains aren't already in one of the customer's segments.
zpa-overlap.why: ZPA matches the most specific segment, so a shared domain would follow the customer's rules, not the POV's.
verify: The detail names the customer's segment that has the domain.
fix: Use the kit's test app, or a domain only the POV uses (Pilot users / ZPA settings).

zpa-pilot.what: The kit looks for the pilot users in ZPA (a SCIM group, or a SAML attribute).
zpa-pilot.why: ZPA takes users from the identity provider, so the access rule needs a ZPA-side way to match them.
verify: ZPA lists the group under the IdP's SCIM groups, or the SAML attribute under its SAML attributes.
fix: Set the SCIM group or SAML attribute in Pilot users (ZPA).

zcc-read.what: The kit reads Client Connector's app and forwarding profiles.
zcc-read.why: The POV copies the default Windows profiles for its own pilot-only profile.
verify: The API client lists Client Connector with view access.
fix: Add Client Connector access from the role spec.

zcc-source.what: The kit looks for a default Windows app profile with a forwarding profile to copy.
zcc-source.why: Without one, the POV's profiles are built by hand (a step for people after Apply).
verify: Search the console menu for App Profiles: a default Windows profile exists.
fix: Nothing to fix: follow the 'Build the POV's Client Connector profiles by hand' step after Apply.

aiguard-read.what: The kit reads AI Guard's apps, policies and rules.
aiguard-read.why: The POV adds its own app and policy next to the customer's, never changing theirs.
verify: The API client lists ZGUARD (AI Guard) with view access.
fix: Add AI Guard access from the role spec.

casb-read.why: The POV's CASB DLP rule scans a connected SaaS tenant.
verify: The API client lists ZIA SaaS security with view access.
fix: Add the access from the role spec.

casb-tenant.what: The kit looks for a connected SaaS tenant.
casb-tenant.why: The CASB criterion needs one to scan.
verify: Search: SaaS Application Tenants. One shows as connected.
fix: Connect one (the step for people, with the SaaS admin's consent).

backup.what: Whether this POV's records (its ledger, approval and change list) are copied, encrypted, to a folder that is synced off this laptop, and when the last copy was made.
backup.why: The ledger is the only record of what the kit created in the customer's tenant. If this laptop is lost or wiped without a backup, the only way back is `pov-kit recover`, which searches the tenant by name. With a backup, a new laptop restores the POV exactly and can still remove everything at the end.
verify: Status > Safety net shows the backup folder and this POV's last backup time.
In that folder there's a file named <pov-id>.zpovbak, updated after each Apply, Fix drift or teardown.
fix: Pick a folder your laptop syncs to the cloud: OneDrive, Google Drive or iCloud Drive (for example ~/OneDrive/pov-backups). Create the folder first.

Choose a passphrase of 12 characters or more and save it in your password manager now: it's what restores the backup on a new laptop. The kit also keeps it in this laptop's keychain so backups run on their own.
Turn on backups below (or Status > Safety net). Every POV on this laptop is backed up straight away, then after every change.
Already set up but 'last backup never'? Back up now below.
backup.retest: Status > Check now: it shows the last backup time.

mcp.what: Whether Claude Desktop on this laptop has the POV's read-only access to the customer's tenant (through Zscaler's own MCP server).
mcp.why: Optional. With it you can ask Claude Desktop things like 'why was Jane blocked?' or 'what did the pilot group use today?' during the POV. It can read but never change anything, and it's removed at handover.
verify: Next steps > Ask Claude about this tenant shows the customer's agreement and 'In Claude Desktop as ...'.
Claude Desktop lists the server after you quit and reopen it.
fix: Ask the customer: Claude Desktop sends what it reads to Anthropic, not through AI Guard, with names as they are. Record who agreed (name and title).
Best practice: ask the customer for a separate view-only API client for it (`pov-kit connect --mcp`), so it never uses the POV's write access.
Add to Claude Desktop, then quit and reopen Claude Desktop.

Optional, with a second agreement from the customer: Let Claude make changes adds a second connector. Claude Desktop can then propose changes (they join the change list for the customer to approve; you Apply), switch the POV's AI Guard policy, run tests and proofs, and Fix drift on the POV's own objects.

plan-approved.what: Whether the change list the customer approved is still what the kit would make from the tenant today.
plan-approved.why: The kit only creates what was approved. If settings, criteria or use cases changed since, the change list changed too and needs a new approval before the next Apply.
verify: Setup > Approval shows who approved which change list (its fingerprint) and when.
fix: Open Setup > Change list, walk the customer through what changed, and record their approval again.

pov-end.what: The POV's end date, and whether POV objects are still in the tenant.
pov-end.why: A POV that ends with its objects still in the customer's tenant leaves rules nobody owns. The kit warns in the last week and fails after the end date.
verify: Setup > Start a POV > More options shows the end date; Status lists the objects still in the tenant.
fix: Extending: `pov-kit set ends YYYY-MM-DD` (or the settings).
Ending: Handover > Remove the POV, or hand the objects over as Terraform.

id-signin.what: How the pilot users sign in: ZIA's own user list (Hosted DB), SAML from the customer's identity provider, or a synced directory; and whether ZIdentity sits in front.
id-signin.why: It decides where the POV's test users can live and how the pilot group reaches ZIA. 'Couldn't tell' means the API client can't read ZIA's sign-in settings; the POV still works, but the kit can't warn about a mismatch.
verify: Search the console menu for Authentication Settings (ZIA): it shows the authentication type.
fix: Give the API client view access to ZIA's authentication settings (role spec), then Run checks again.
Or ignore it: this check only informs.

id-testusers.what: Where the POV's test users are created: in ZIA's own user list, or in ZIdentity when the tenant keeps its users there.
id-testusers.why: Test users let the POV run without the customer's real accounts. Their passwords are generated and kept only in this laptop's keychain.
verify: Next steps > Test users lists them, with Show password.
In the console, search for Users: each is named with the POV's prefix.
fix: Nothing to fix. To use real people instead, change Pilot users and approve the new change list.
ZPA takes users from the identity provider, so ZPA can't use test users.

zia-scope.what: Whether every POV rule still applies only to the pilot group.
zia-scope.why: A POV rule that applies to more people changes their internet access, which the customer never approved.
verify: Open each rule named in the detail: Users/Groups shows only the pilot group.
fix: Status > Fix drift puts the scope back (only on the POV's own rules).

*-present.what: Whether every object the POV created is still in the tenant, as the ledger records it.
*-present.why: If someone deletes or renames a POV object, its criteria can't be proved and teardown can't find it.
verify: The detail lists any missing object; search the console for its name.
fix: Status > Fix drift recreates missing POV objects (it never touches the customer's).

*-left.what: Whether any POV object is still in the tenant after teardown.
verify: The detail names what's left; search the console for it.
fix: Handover > Remove the POV again (it retries), or delete the object by hand and Check now.

zia-disabled.what: Whether a POV rule was disabled in the console.
verify: Open the rule: its state is Enabled.
fix: Status > Fix drift enables it again.

zia-foreign.what: Objects using the POV's name prefix that the POV didn't create.
zia-foreign.why: The kit leaves them alone; they may confuse who owns what.
verify: Search the console for the names in the detail.
fix: Nothing to do unless they're left over from an earlier POV: then remove that POV (or the objects) by hand.

aiguard-key.what: Whether the POV's AI Guard detection key is in this laptop's keychain.
aiguard-key.why: The kit scans test prompts with it. AI Guard shows a key's secret only once, when it's created.
verify: AI Guard tab: tests run without a key error.
fix: Delete the key named 'ZPOV: POV detection key' in AI Guard, then Status > Fix drift makes a new one and keeps its secret.

zpa-connectors.what: How many of the POV's App Connectors are enrolled and connected.
zpa-connectors.why: ZPA reaches the POV's app only through them.
verify: Search the console for App Connectors: two in the POV's group show Connected.
fix: Deploy them (Finish setup > Deploy the POV's App Connectors); allow 10 to 15 minutes; they need outbound TCP 443.

zdx-read.what: The kit reads ZDX with the POV's API client.
zdx-read.why: ZDX criteria need the pilot devices' scores and probes.
verify: The POV's API client has a ZDX role.
fix: Give the client a view-only ZDX role (the step for people 'Give the API client a ZDX role').

zdx-app.what: Whether ZDX already monitors an app the POV can deep-trace.
zdx-app.why: Deep traces measure a monitored app from each pilot device; without one, DX-SCR-01 has nothing to show.
verify: Search the console for ZDX Applications: at least one app is being monitored.
fix: Monitor an app in ZDX (Microsoft 365 or Zoom are typical), or pick one with `pov-kit set zdx.app NAME`.

zdx-users.what: Whether the kit knows the pilot users, to find their devices in ZDX.
zdx-users.why: Deep traces start on the pilot devices only.
verify: Pilot users lists names or test accounts.
fix: Name the pilot users, or apply the POV's test accounts, then run the checks again.

zdx-devices.what: Whether pilot devices report to ZDX (in the last 24 hours).
zdx-devices.why: ZDX scores and deep traces come from the devices.
verify: ZDX lists each pilot device.
fix: Set up the pilot devices (Finish setup); Client Connector with ZDX reports within an hour.

zdx-traces.what: How many baseline deep traces the POV has started on pilot devices.
zdx-traces.why: They're the before/after evidence for DX-SCR-01.
verify: ZDX > Diagnostics (search: Deep Tracing) lists them for the pilot devices.
fix: They start once pilot devices report to ZDX: set up the devices, then Status > Fix drift starts any that are missing.

customer-actions.what: The steps only the customer can do (in the change list), and which aren't confirmed yet.
customer-actions.why: Their criteria can't pass until they're done.
verify: Setup > Finish setup and Next steps > Steps for people show each, with its check.
fix: Open Finish setup and check or mark each one.
